laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Sy ken elke kind se naam en ook die kinders wat nooit boeke uitneem nie.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Sy ken elke kind se naam, ook die name van die kinders wat nooit boeke uitneem nie.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: As written she knows every name 'and also the children', which joins two unlike objects; the intended point is that she also knows the names of children who never borrow books.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original says she knows the children themselves who never borrow books, not only their names; the proposal narrows that to names, so the meaning moves.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: skuif elke keer die boek oor trekkers nader sonder om te vra
laat_vaar_vorige.na: skuif elke keer die boek oor trekkers nader na hom toe sonder om te vra
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'nader' does not say closer to whom; 'na hom toe' makes clear the book is moved towards Sipho, which is what the sentence means.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Nader skuif' is idiomatic and the context already makes clear it moves towards Sipho; the addition only lengthens the sentence.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Op 'n Dinsdag sit Naledi op die mat met 'n dik boek oor slange.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Op 'n Dinsdag sit Naledi met 'n dik boek oor slange op die mat.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: In Afrikaans the manner phrase normally comes before the place phrase; the current order reads as if the mat has the book.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original reads naturally, and the proposal creates a worse ambiguity ('slange op die mat' reads as snakes on the mat).

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Sy sit haar stempel neer en sy bly stil
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Sy sit haar stempel neer en bly stil
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The repeated subject 'sy' is unnecessary and makes the sentence wooden; dropping it gives one sentence with two verbs and needs no comma.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The repeated 'sy' is normal Afrikaans and part of the story's rhythm; the original does not genuinely jar, so this is a lateral move.
